summary: Regional GPU thin window caused by high-frequency short streams from customer sidecar
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Nimbus Analytics, dedicated tier) reports repeated elevated p95/p99 latency and intermittent 429s for their reserved slice in us-west-2 during the 09:00-11:30 PDT window on 2026-03-10. Impact: multiple live product features degraded; observed client retries and a spike in error rate; customer flagged as impacting production SLAs.

Impact:
- Increased p99 latency from baseline 220ms to 1.1s for text generation routes pinned to redwood-open-7b-v2.
- ~15% of requests received 429s or queued fallback to hosted tier.
- Customer experienced user-visible errors causing degraded UX during morning traffic.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved slice (customer_id: nimbus-847) in us-west-2.
- Model variants: redwood-open-7b-v2 (quantized), embedding route tiny-embed-1.
- Autoscaler configuration: conservative smoothing window (60s), cooldown 120s.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer runs many short-lived connections (median 350ms per stream) from a sidecar-based ingest pipeline that opens ~200 concurrent short streams in bursts.
2) Short streams produce high connect/disconnect churn and many small token batches.
3) Serving allocator holds partial reservations on GPU slots for connections in warmup state; allocator credit drains and slot fragmentation increases.
4) Autoscaler signal (smoothed aggregated throughput) underreports transient spike; autoscaler fails to scale quickly.

Logs / traces: (excerpt)
- sidecar@customer: repeated connection bursts 09:04:12 - 09:04:46 (200->650 short streams)
- serving-runtime: WARN allocator: partial_slot_hold tenant=nimbus-847 slot_frag=0.36
- autoscaler: DEBUG smoothing: observed_spike=720 req/s smoothed=210 req/s
- metrics: p99=1.12s, error_rate=12%, 429_count=98/min during peak

Initial customer-facing message:
"We're seeing intermittent high latencies and spikes of 429s in the morning window. Only impacts our dedicated slice in us-west-2. Can you advise?"
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 09:10: Initial pager triggered by support after customer Slack (#support-nimbus).
- 09:25: SRE confirmed reserved slice p99 spike and elevated 429s.
- 09:40: Correlated with customer sidecar connection bursts via netflow and request-id mapping.
- 10:05: Observed allocator partial_slot_hold logs and slot fragmentation metrics.

Hypotheses tested:
1) Noisy neighbor from other tenants in the same cluster — rejected: tenant isolation metrics show heavy activity originates from nimbus-847 sidecar agents.
2) Autoscaler smoothing window masking short spikes — confirmed: raw throughput signal shows 3x spike but smoothed metric kept low, delaying scale-out.
3) Driver/hardware thermal throttling — rejected: host telemetry normal, GPU utilization moderate but fragmented.

Key findings:
- Short high-frequency streams cause frequent small-batch allocations and partial slot reservations. These partial reservations increase slot fragmentation and reduce effective bin-packing efficiency.
- The autoscaler uses an averaged throughput signal (60s window) leading to delayed scale-out for bursts lasting <60s.
- The allocator credit mechanism drains because connections hold prefetch reservations during warmup, preventing reuse for other tenants and creating a temporary thin window for GPU availability.

Data / dashboards referenced:
- /dashboards/dedicated/us-west/allocator-slot-fragmentation (spike correlated at 09:04)
- /dashboards/autoscale/smoothing-vs-raw (shows smoothing mask)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged, created incident channel #inc-nimbus-gpu. Asking for immediate logs and customer traffic pattern details.
2026-03-10 09:28 - SRE (Jonah Kim): Confirmed p99 spike in reserved slice, starting correlation with customer's request-ids. Partial slot holds visible in allocator logs.

2026-03-10 09:45 - Customer (Nimbus Eng - Elena Ortiz): Provided sidecar telemetry and confirmed they deploy a bursty ingest pattern triggered by scheduled batch windows. Willing to throttle as workaround.

2026-03-10 10:10 - Ravi Menon (On-call SRE): Deployed temporary rate-limit for customer sidecar at edge (100 rps cap) and issued a sidecar restart recommendation to customer to prevent continuous connect churn.
2026-03-10 10:35 - Megan Liu (Support): Notified customer of mitigation; monitoring metrics for recovery.

2026-03-11 11:00 - Engineering (Priya Das): Proposed medium-term changes: reduce autoscaler smoothing window for dedicated slices to 15s (configurable per-tenant) and add token-bucket per-connection reservation upper bound to reduce partial_slot_hold.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Customer (Elena Ortiz): Applied client-side throttle and confirmed latency returned to baseline; requested timeline for permanent fixes.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: edged rate-limit (100 rps) on customer's sidecar and customer applied client-side throttle; sidecar restart cleared connection churn. Result: p99 returned to baseline within 25 minutes and 429s dropped to <1% of baseline.

Permanent actions planned:
- Adjust autoscaler configuration for dedicated slices: reduce default smoothing window to 15s for bursty patterns and add an override toggle per-reservation (ENG-1614).
- Implement allocator change to enforce per-connection reservation caps to avoid long partial_slot_hold (runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1845).
- Customer-facing guidance: updated best-practices doc for sidecar connection pooling and suggested using multiplexed long-lived streams instead of many short streams.

Follow-ups:
- ENG to track PRs and rollout via canary to us-west-2 (owner: Priya Das, ETA 2 weeks).
- CS to coordinate with Nimbus for traffic-shaping guidance and post-deploy verification (owner: Megan Liu).
- Ops to add an alert for slot_fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 on dedicated pools.

Status: Monitoring after mitigation; actions scheduled and linked PR opened.
next_steps:
1) ENG: land autoscaler smoothing override and allocator reservation cap PRs (ENG-1614, runtime PR/1845).
2) OPS: create alert for slot_fragmentation_ratio and add runbook steps for noisy-sidecar mitigation.
3) CS: organize post-mitigation verification with Nimbus next morning window.
4) Document: publish sidecar best-practices and include recommended throttle configs for dedicated slices.
customer_impact_summary: Major impact during morning burst window: customer reported degraded UX and increased errors. Temporary mitigation restored service; customer requested timeline for permanent fixes and assurances for future morning windows.
